## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the $C^2$ geometry of [[def-bem-smooth-helmholtz-combined-field-operator]]. For each fixed $k>0$ and real $\eta\ne0$, its operator extends boundedly to complex $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ and
$$A_{k,\eta}=\tfrac12I+K_k-i\eta V_k,\qquad V_k=\gamma S_k,$$
where both $K_k$ and the restriction $V_k:H^{1/2}(\Gamma)\to H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ are compact. Thus $2A_{k,\eta}=I-\mathcal K_{k,\eta}$ with compact $\mathcal K_{k,\eta}=-2K_k+2i\eta V_k$. No uniform estimate in $k$ is asserted.

1.1 In surface coordinates put $r=|x-y|$. The $C^2$ graph bounds give $|n_y\cdot(x-y)|\le Cr^2$ and $|n_y-n_x|\le Cr$. Therefore both kernels $L_V=G_k(x-y)$ and $L_K=\partial_{n_y}G_k(x-y)$ satisfy $|L(x,y)|\le C/r$. Their first target-coordinate derivatives satisfy $|\partial_xL|\le C/r^2$: for $K$, differentiating the numerator tangentially gives $n_y\cdot t_x=(n_y-n_x)\cdot t_x=O(r)$, and differentiating the radial factors gives at worst $O(r^2)O(r^{-4})$. Fixed $k$ only changes the constants. Localize targets and sources by chart cutoffs; for near-diagonal pieces use a common graph chart and absorb its bounded surface Jacobian into the source kernel. Off-diagonal pieces have bounded first target derivatives. Each resulting chart kernel $l(z,w)$, extended with cutoffs by zero, thus has size $C/|z-w|$ and target derivative size $C/|z-w|^2$. [F1, F2, F91, given, algebra]

3.1 For any $0<s<1$, integrate the square of the last translation bound against $|h|^{-2-2s}dh$ for $|h|<1$; polar coordinates give the finite integral $C\int_0^1r^{1-2s}(1+|\log r|)^2dr$. The $|h|\ge1$ part is bounded by the $L^2$ estimate. Hence each localized $T$ maps $L^2$ boundedly to $H^s$ in the difference norm, in particular for $s=3/4$. To check the equivalent Fourier norm directly, apply Plancherel to differences and Tonelli: the inner integral $\int|e^{2\pi i\xi\cdot h}-1|^2|h|^{-2-2s}dh$ equals $c_s|\xi|^{2s}$ by scaling and rotation, with $0<c_s<\infty$ since near zero the numerator is $O(|h|^2)$ and at infinity it is bounded. This also identifies the half-order norm in [F3]. [F3, F90, step 2.1, given, algebra]

Therefore $A_{k,\eta}=\tfrac12I+K_k-i\eta V_k$, and its displayed compact perturbation follows by addition and scalar multiplication of the compact maps just proved. 4.1 A bounded family of functions supported in a fixed compact chart and bounded in $H^{3/4}$ is precompact in $H^{1/2}$. Here is a direct verification. For a smooth compactly supported mollifier $\rho_\epsilon$, $|1-\widehat\rho(\epsilon\xi)|\le C\min(\epsilon|\xi|,1)$ and thus $\|f-\rho_\epsilon*f\|_{H^{1/2}}\le C\epsilon^{1/4}\|f\|_{H^{3/4}}$ by the Fourier weights. For fixed $\epsilon$, the convolutions and their first two derivatives are uniformly bounded and have one fixed bounded support, by Cauchy–Schwarz with the fixed derivatives of $\rho_\epsilon$. They are precompact in $C^1$ on a containing rectangle: choose increasingly fine finite grids, take convergent subsequences of the finitely many value and first-derivative samples, and use the uniform first/second derivative bounds to extend sample convergence uniformly. A diagonal subsequence gives convergence of both values and first derivatives. Uniform $C^1$ convergence on a fixed compact support implies $H^{1/2}$ convergence, since the difference-norm integrand near the diagonal is bounded by $\|\nabla f\|_\infty^2|z-w|^{-1}$ and away from the diagonal by a constant times $\|f\|_\infty^2|z-w|^{-3}$. The uniform mollification error now gives finite nets for the original family in $H^{1/2}$, hence compact closure in its complete Hilbert norm. [F3, step 3.1, given, algebra, construct]

## Definition

For two admissible states $U_L,U_R\in\mathcal G$, let $\bar U=(U_L+U_R)/2$, $\Delta v=v(U_R)-v(U_L)$, and $\Delta\psi_j=\psi_j(U_R)-\psi_j(U_L)$, where $v$ and $\psi_j$ are given by [[lem-compressible-ideal-gas-entropy-pair-and-variables]]. Define the symmetric two-point flux

$$F_j^{\mathrm{ec}}(U_L,U_R)= \begin{cases} F_j(U_L),&\Delta v=0,\\[2mm] F_j(\bar U)+\dfrac{\Delta\psi_j-\Delta v^TF_j(\bar U)}{\|\Delta v\|^2}\,\Delta v,&\Delta v\ne0. \end{cases}$$

The norm is Euclidean in the $d+2$ conservative-state coordinates. The convexity result [[lem-compressible-admissible-state-set-open-convex]] ensures $\bar U\in\mathcal G$.

## Statement

Let $u\in C^1([0,T];C^2(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R^m))$ solve $u_t=D\Delta u+F(u)$, with constant diagonal $D=\operatorname{diag}(d_i)$, and let its range lie in $R$. Let $c$ be a conservation or dissipation vector on $R$. One may take (i) a box $\Omega=\prod_{j=1}^d[0,L_j]$ with periodic identification or homogeneous Neumann data, or (ii) a bounded domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, with a specified finite piecewise $C^1$ boundary presentation as in [[def-bounded-piecewise-c-one-euclidean-domain]], assuming $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ in this second branch and homogeneous Neumann data on every face outside the edge set. For either branch,
$$
\frac{d}{dt}\int_\Omega c^Tu(x,t)\,dx=\int_\Omega c^TF(u(x,t))\,dx.
$$
Hence the total mass is constant when $c^TF=0$ on $R$ and nonincreasing when $c^TF\le0$ on $R$. The first branch is choice-free; $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used only for the stated piecewise $C^1$ divergence-theorem branch.

1.1 Since $u_t$ is continuous on the compact cylinder, the time difference quotient of $c^Tu$ is the time average of $c^Tu_t$ by [F4], and uniform continuity makes it converge uniformly to $c^Tu_t$. Each stated domain has finite volume, so integrating this uniform convergence proves $\frac d{dt}\int_\Omega c^Tu=\int_\Omega c^Tu_t$. [F4, given, algebra]

2.1 In the box branch, substitute [F1] into step 1.1. The diffusion contribution is $\sum_i c_id_i\int_\Omega\Delta u_i\,dx$. For each coordinate $j$, [F3] permits integration in $x_j$ first, and [F4] gives $\int_0^{L_j}\partial_{jj}u_i\,dx_j=\partial_ju_i|_{x_j=L_j}-\partial_ju_i|_{x_j=0}$. This difference is zero for matching periodic traces and is zero for homogeneous Neumann data. Summing over components and coordinates makes the total diffusion contribution vanish. [A1, F1, F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

## Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $\widehat\Omega=(-1,1)^2$, let $\Phi(x,y)=(x,y+x^2/4)$, and let $\Phi_h$ be its continuous piecewise-affine nodal interpolant on a shape-regular matching triangular mesh with maximum diameter $h\le1$, small enough that $J_h=\det D\Phi_h\ge1/2$ as in [[lem-parabolic-domain-map-approximation]]. Put $J=\det D\Phi$ and define the pulled-back Laplace tensors $$B=J D\Phi^{-1}D\Phi^{-T},\qquad B_h=J_hD\Phi_h^{-1}D\Phi_h^{-T}.$$ On $V=H^1_0(\widehat\Omega)$ set $$a(v,w)=\int_{\widehat\Omega}
abla v^TB
abla w,\qquad a_h(v,w)=\int_{\widehat\Omega}
abla v^TB_h
abla w.$$ Let $V_h$ be the finite-dimensional space of continuous functions on $\overline{\widehat\Omega}$ that are affine on each triangle and vanish on $\partial\widehat\Omega$, viewed as a subspace of $V$. Suppose $a$ and $a_h$ are uniformly bounded and coercive on $V$ and $V_h$, respectively, with constants independent of $h$, $F\in V^*$ and $F_h\in V_h^*$ are bounded, $u\in H^2(\widehat\Omega)\cap V$ is real-valued and satisfies $a(u,w)=F(w)$ for every $w\in V$, and $u_h\in V_h$ satisfies $a_h(u_h,w_h)=F_h(w_h)$ for every $w_h\in V_h$.

If a common physical boundary lift $G\in C^2$ with bounded first and second derivatives on a convex neighborhood of the two geometry images is used, let $\ell_{\partial,h}$ be its pulled-back residual from [[lem-curved-boundary-lift-residual]] and set $\epsilon_{\partial,h}=\|\ell_{\partial,h}\|_{V^*}$. Assume the load difference on $V_h$ splits as $$ (F-F_h)|_{V_h}=L_{\mathrm{bulk},h}+\ell_{\partial,h}|_{V_h},\qquad \|L_{\mathrm{bulk},h}\|_{V_h^*}\le\epsilon_{F,h}^{\mathrm{bulk}},\qquad \epsilon_{F,h}^{\mathrm{bulk}}\ge0.$$ Here the $V^*$ and $V_h^*$ norms are induced by the $H^1$ norm. If no lift is used, set $\ell_{\partial,h}=0$ and take the same bound for the full load difference. Then $$\|u-u_h\|_{H^1(\widehat\Omega)}\le C igl(h\|u\|_{H^2(\widehat\Omega)}+\epsilon_{F,h}^{\mathrm{bulk}}+\epsilon_{\partial,h} igr).$$ where $C$ is independent of $h$. For the parabolic geometry family, $\epsilon_{\partial,h}\le C_G(e_0+e_1)\le C_Gh$.

1.1 The exact shear has positive determinant, and [F1] gives $J_h\ge1/2$; thus both tensor formulas are defined almost everywhere. By [L1] and [F8], $V=H^1_0(\widehat\Omega)$ is Hilbert in the stated $H^1$ norm. The boundedness and coercivity assumptions, bounded loads, finite-dimensional conforming subspace $V_h\subset V$, and the given variational equations supply the remaining hypotheses of [F5]. [A1, F1, F5, F8, L1, given]

1.3 By [L2], the shape-regular matching mesh satisfies the affine scaling hypotheses in [F3]. Apply [F3] on each triangle with the identity geometry map. The finite element interpolants assemble into the global nodal interpolant $I_hu$, and [F4] gives $I_hu\in V_h$. Squaring each local estimate, summing over cells, and using $h_K\le h$ gives $\|u-I_hu\|_{H^1}\le Ch\|u\|_{H^2}$. Since $h\le1$, [L1] gives $\|I_hu\|_{H^1}\le\|u\|_{H^1}+Ch\|u\|_{H^2}\le C\|u\|_{H^2}$. [F3, F4, A1, A2, L1, L2, given, algebra]

## Statement

For exact policy evaluations, every strict switch in
[[alg-na-finite-control-howard-policy-iteration]] weakly increases the policy
value at every state and strictly increases it at each switched state. No
deterministic policy can recur after a strict switch. With budget
$P=\prod_i|A_i|$, the algorithm terminates within $P$ policy evaluations at
the unique solution of the Bellman system in
[[def-na-finite-state-discounted-bellman-system]]. A smaller budget may return

[F1, F3, step 2.1, algebra]

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the neutral finite configuration and full-rank cell of
[[def-ewald-three-dimensional-periodic-source-data]]. Let
$Q=\sum_i|q_i|$, choose real and reciprocal cutoffs $R,K\ge1$, and put
$M_R=\lfloor R\rfloor$, $M_K=\lfloor K\rfloor$. Let $C_R=C_A$ be the shell
constant for $\Lambda=A\mathbb Z^3$ and $C_K=C_{2\pi A^{-T}}$ the shell constant
for the angular reciprocal lattice. For the real-space cutoff, retain all
$(i,j,\lambda)$ with $|x_i-x_j+\lambda|\le R$ except $(i,i,0)$. For the
reciprocal cutoff, retain all $k\ne0$ with $|\kappa_k|\le K$. Use the
$T_3(\beta,M)$ controller of
[[lem-ewald-lattice-shell-gaussian-tail-controllers]]. Then the omitted tails
in the exact Ewald potential, energy, and particle force satisfy
$$B_R^U=\frac{QC_R}{\sqrt\pi\alpha}T_3(\alpha^2,M_R),\qquad B_R^E=\frac{Q^2C_R}{2\sqrt\pi\alpha}T_3(\alpha^2,M_R),$$
$$B_R^{F,i}=\frac{|q_i|QC_R}{\sqrt\pi}(2\alpha+\alpha^{-1}) T_3(\alpha^2,M_R),$$
and
$$B_K^U=\frac{4\pi QC_K}{V}T_3((4\alpha^2)^{-1},M_K),\qquad B_K^E=\frac{2\pi Q^2C_K}{V}T_3((4\alpha^2)^{-1},M_K),$$
$$B_K^{F,i}=\frac{4\pi|q_i|QC_K}{V} T_3((4\alpha^2)^{-1},M_K).$$
For a certified finite value, replace each $T_3$ by the corresponding finite
upper controller $U_3$. The real force is evaluated only away from collisions;
no field bound is asserted at a point source.

The exact force is the negative gradient of the renormalized energy. With
$r_{ij\lambda}=|x_i-x_j+\lambda|$ and $a_k(t_i)=e^{-i\kappa_k\cdot x_i}$,
it is
$$F_i=-q_i\sum_{j=1}^n\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}'q_j\phi_s'(r_{ij\lambda})\frac{x_i-x_j+\lambda}{r_{ij\lambda}}-q_i\sum_{k\ne0}c_k\operatorname{Re}(\overline{\sigma_k}\nabla_xa_k(t_i)).$$
The prime excludes only $(j,\lambda)=(i,0)$; the absolutely convergent
reciprocal sum is real by pairing $k$ and $-k$.

1.1 Fix a collision-free configuration and choose a small closed product of coordinate balls around its source positions, using local torus lifts, that remains collision-free. Finitely many nearby nonself images then stay a positive distance from the singularity. For large real-space shell index $m$, [F1] bounds the kernel by a constant times $e^{-\alpha^2m^2}$ and its first position derivatives by $(2\alpha+\alpha^{-1})e^{-\alpha^2m^2}/\sqrt\pi$. [F2] bounds the shell count uniformly over every translate; since the source-difference vectors stay in a bounded set, $|\lambda|\to\infty$ forces the corresponding distance to infinity uniformly. Thus the real energy series and each first-derivative series converge uniformly on this product. Finite partial sums are continuously differentiable and their values converge at one point by [F4]. Under [A1], apply [F5] along each real coordinate line to justify termwise differentiation of the real energy. [A1, F1, F2, F4, F5]

1.2 For the reciprocal energy, [F3] gives $|\sigma_k|\le Q$ and Gaussian decay of $c_k$, while [F6] gives $|\nabla_{x_i}\sigma_k|=|q_i||\kappa_k|$. The derivative of each summand $\frac12c_k|\sigma_k|^2$ is bounded by $c_kQ|q_i||\kappa_k|$. All nonzero modes in shells $m\ge1$ therefore have a summable position-uniform majorant $C(m+1)^3e^{-m^2/(4\alpha^2)}$ by [F2]; the remaining bounded ball contains finitely many modes because the reciprocal lattice is full rank. The energy summands themselves are bounded by $Q^2c_k/2$, whose shell sum also converges by [F2]–[F3]. Thus the reciprocal energy and all its first-derivative series converge uniformly on the same product. Finite partial sums have values converging at one point by [F4], so [F5] gives their termwise derivatives along every coordinate line. [A1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6]

## Statement

Let $Q$ be a full-dimensional convex polytope in $\mathbb R^4$ with $m\ge5$ vertices. A facet is a three-dimensional face, and a vertex is an extreme point. Then the number $f_3$ of facets satisfies
$$f_3\le \frac{m(m-3)}2.$$

1.1 Fix a vertex $v$ of $Q$ and let $C$ be the convex hull of its other vertices. Since $v$ is extreme, $v\notin C$. The finite convex hull $C$ is compact, so choose $q\in C$ minimizing $\|v-q\|$. For every $y\in C$ and $0<t\le1$, $q+t(y-q)\in C$, hence $\|v-q-t(y-q)\|^2\ge\|v-q\|^2$. Expanding, dividing by $t$, and letting $t\downarrow0$ gives $(v-q)\cdot(y-q)\le0$. Therefore $\ell(x)=(v-q)\cdot x$ satisfies $\ell(v)-\ell(y)\ge\|v-q\|^2>0$ for every $y\in C$. Choose $\delta>0$ smaller than every positive gap $\ell(v)-\ell(u)$ over the other vertices. The section $Q_v=Q\cap\{\ell=\ell(v)-\delta\}$ cuts exactly the edges incident to $v$ and is a three-dimensional convex polytope; its vertices correspond to those edges, and its facets correspond to the facets of $Q$ containing $v$. Write $d_v,t_v$ for the numbers of vertices and facets of $Q_v$. [given, choose, construct, algebra]

2.1 Choose a facet $F_0$ of $Q_v$ and a viewpoint just outside its relative interior in the open region that gives a Schlegel projection onto the plane of $F_0$. Convexity makes the projected facets cover $F_0$: each ray from the viewpoint through an interior point of $F_0$ enters $Q_v$ there and has a unique last intersection with its boundary. The exit point lies on a non-base facet; uniqueness of that exit makes projected facet interiors disjoint, and shared edges project to shared boundaries. Choose the viewpoint generically within this open region so projected vertices are distinct and no three projected vertices are collinear. For each pair or triple of vertices, the forbidden coincidence or collinearity condition is a nonzero polynomial equation in the viewpoint coordinates: a pair coincidence forces the viewpoint onto their line, and a triple collinearity forces it into the plane through those three noncollinear vertices. A nonzero polynomial cannot vanish on an open set (in one variable it has finitely many roots; induction on the variables applied to its coefficient polynomials proves the claim), so finitely many forbidden sets cannot exhaust the region. Triangulate each projected convex polygonal facet by joining one vertex to its nonadjacent vertices. This yields a triangulation of $F_0$ with $d_v$ sites and $k_v$ hull sites, where $k_v$ is the number of vertices of $F_0$ and $k_v\ge3$. [step 1.1, construct, choose, algebra]

## Definition

Input an exact dyadic real $x$, positive rational absolute tolerance
$\varepsilon_a$, optional positive rational relative tolerance
$\varepsilon_r$, a fixed exponent range $(e_{\min},e_{\max})$, and finite
positive integer caps $S_{\max},D_{\max},N_{\max},p_{\max},W$, with
$p_{\max}\ge2$. Here
$S_{\max}$ bounds stages, $D_{\max}$ the continued-fraction depth,
$N_{\max}$ the asymptotic truncation, $p_{\max}$ the dyadic precision, and
$W$ the exact interval operations, terms, and subroutine calls performed by
this procedure. Reject nonpositive tolerances, invalid caps,
$e_{\min}>e_{\max}$, or $x\le0$ with domain. At stage $q$, use
$D=\min(q,D_{\max})$, $N=\min(q,N_{\max})$, precision
$p=\max(2,\min(q,p_{\max}))$, and truncation index $q$ for elementary-range calls.
Outputs and status meanings are those of
[[def-certified-evaluation-result-contract]].

All rational and interval arithmetic uses
[[def-outward-rounded-interval-and-ball-operations]]. Charge every exact
arithmetic operation, range-evaluator node operation, term, rounding, and
loop update to the shared counter $W$. Interrupt any nested elementary-range
call with inconclusive before its next operation would exceed the remaining
budget. Return inconclusive before any local operation would exceed $W$. A
final endpoint overflow
returns range. A non-finite required arithmetic operation or elementary-range subcall makes its candidate unavailable; if neither candidate can be formed, the current stage is
inconclusive and later stages may still be tried.

For each stage $q=1,\ldots,S_{\max}$, compute $P_q$, a finite dyadic
interval containing $\pi$, as follows. For $r\in\{1/5,1/239\}$, form
$A_q(r)=\sum_{j=0}^{q-1}(-1)^jr^{2j+1}/(2j+1)$ and
$E_q(r)=r^{2q+1}/((2q+1)(1-r^2))$ exactly; the arctangent-tail lemma gives
$\arctan r\in[A_q(r)-E_q(r),A_q(r)+E_q(r)]$. Combine these intervals by
$\pi=16\arctan(1/5)-4\arctan(1/239)$ and round outward to the selected
format at precision $p$. The Machin identity and tails are supplied by
[[lem-trigonometric-identities-machin-and-range-reduction]]. If the interval
conversion is non-finite, skip the stage. Call
[[alg-certified-elementary-range-evaluation]] on the real one-node DAG
$\sqrt{P_q}$, using exponent range $(e_{\min},e_{\max})$, precision $p$,
and truncation $q$. If this call is not finite or its output $R_q$ does
not have positive lower endpoint, skip this stage. Otherwise $R_q$ encloses
$\sqrt\pi$ by [[thm-real-elementary-range-enclosures]].

Form the continued-fraction candidate as follows. Set
$I_D=[0,(D+1)/(2x)]$. For $k=D-1,\ldots,0$, set
$$I_k=\left[\frac{k+1}{2(x+\sup I_{k+1})}, \frac{k+1}{2(x+\inf I_{k+1})}\right]$$
by outward interval operations. Apply the decreasing map
$r\mapsto1/(\sqrt\pi(x+r))$ to $I_0$, evaluating $\sqrt\pi$ with
$R_q$, to obtain a candidate interval $C_q$. The finite-depth
containment lemma [[lem-erfcx-continued-fraction-enclosure]] makes $C_q$
a valid enclosure for every $D\ge0$.

If $N\ge1$, also form the asymptotic candidate. Evaluate
$$S_N(x)=\frac1{x\sqrt\pi}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}(-1)^k\frac{(1/2)_k}{x^{2k}}, \qquad B_N(x)=\frac1{x\sqrt\pi}\frac{(2N)!}{4^NN!x^{2N}}$$
with $R_q$ and exact factorial/rational interval arithmetic. Write the computed sum interval as $[s_-,s_+]$ and take a nonnegative outward upper endpoint $b_N$ for the remainder bound $B_N$. Set
$A_q=[s_-,s_++b_N]$ when $N$ is even and
$A_q=[s_--b_N,s_+]$ when $N$ is odd, rounding the final endpoints outward. The signed remainder lemma
[[lem-erfcx-asymptotic-remainder]] makes $A_q$ a valid enclosure.

If both candidates are finite, intersect them when the intersection is
nonempty; if it is empty, discard the stage. If only one is finite, use that
candidate. Round the selected final endpoints outward to precision $p$.
Return success at the first stage whose radius is at most
$\varepsilon_a$. Set relative_certified to true exactly when relative
tolerance was requested, the interval excludes zero, and the contract's
relative-radius test passes; a failed relative test does not prevent absolute
success. If no stage passes before the finite caps, return inconclusive.

## Definition

Inputs are a finite dyadic complex rectangle $Z$, a target label $\Gamma$ or
$\ell$, positive exact rational absolute tolerance $\varepsilon_a$,
optional positive exact rational relative tolerance $\varepsilon_r$, a fixed
dyadic format precision $p_0\ge2$ and exponent range
$(e_{\min},e_{\max})$, fixed integer elementary truncation index $K\ge1$,
finite positive integer work cap $W$, and integer precision cap $P\ge p_0$.
The target
$\ell$ is the continued
branch in [[def-loggamma-slit-plane-branch]]. Reject an invalid target, empty or non-finite rectangle, invalid cap,
tolerance, $e_{\min}>e_{\max}$, or
$Z\not\subset\mathbb C\setminus(-\infty,0]$ by returning
domain. The exact rectangle test is: either the imaginary interval omits
zero, or the real interval has strictly positive lower endpoint. Reject a
selected shift $m>W$ with inconclusive. For stages $q=1,\ldots,P$, use
precision $p=\max(p_0,q)$, harmonic cutoff $M=\min(q,W)$, product cutoff
$N=\min(q,W)$, and the fixed elementary truncation index $K$ for every
range call. Output statuses are those of
[[def-certified-evaluation-result-contract]].

Use [[def-outward-rounded-interval-and-ball-operations]] for interval
arithmetic. Count every exact rational or interval operation, series term,
elementary-DAG node operation, rounding, and loop update against the shared
counter $W$. If the procedure is called by another evaluator, charge these

## Example

On one tetrahedron, compare the naive vector nodal space $[P_1(K)]^3$ with the compatible scalar-to-edge gradient map $\nabla W_h^0$ of [[def-na-lowest-order-whitney-de-rham-spaces]]. The vector field $v(x)=x_1e_1$ lies in the nodal vector space, has zero curl, and is not the gradient of a continuous piecewise-affine scalar. Thus the naive nodal curl-curl matrix has a zero-energy mode outside that compatible gradient image. This identifies a discrete kernel mismatch; it does not claim that gradients are absent from the continuum curl kernel.

1.1 The field $v(x)=(x_1,0,0)$ is vector-valued affine, so it belongs to $[P_1(K)]^3$. Its componentwise curl is zero because its only nonzero component depends only on $x_1$. Hence $(\operatorname{curl}v,\operatorname{curl}v)_{L^2(K)}=0$. [A1, given, F2, algebra]

$$u=z+\nabla p,\qquad \|z\|_{H^1(\Omega)}+\|p-p_\Omega\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\le C_\Omega\|u\|_{H(\operatorname{curl};\Omega)}.$$
Here $H_0(\operatorname{curl})$ is the closure definition of [[def-na-zero-tangential-hcurl]], and $p_\Omega=|\Omega|^{-1}\int_\Omega p$ fixes the additive constant. The constant may depend on the domain but not on a mesh.

## Statement

Let $N\ge2$ be even, $d\ge1$, $h=1/N$, and use the staggered operators
from [[def-na-periodic-staggered-grid-stokes-operators]]. Put
$q_j=(-1)^{j_1}$, so $q\in Q_h$, and let $\nu,k>0$. Start one step of
[[alg-na-periodic-incremental-pressure-correction]] from $u^n=0$, $p^n=0$
with
$$ f^{n+1}=k^{-1}G_hq+\nu A_hG_hq. $$
Then the unique predictor is $\widetilde u^{n+1}=G_hq$, the pressure
increment is $\phi^{n+1}=k^{-1}q$, and the corrected velocity is exactly
$u^{n+1}=0$. The pressure update is $p^{n+1}=k^{-1}q$.

1.1 Since $N$ is even, $q$ has zero mean. The staggered gradient is not zero: $(G_hq)_{1,j}=-2q_j/h$. Also $\Delta_hq=-4q/h^2$, so [F1] gives $D_hG_hq=\Delta_hq$. Periodic summation shows both $G_hq$ and $A_hG_hq$ have zero component means, hence the force is admissible. [F1, given, algebra]

2.1 Substituting $\widetilde u^{n+1}=G_hq$ and $u^n=p^n=0$ into the predictor equation [F2] gives $k^{-1}G_hq+\nu A_hG_hq=f^{n+1}$, so uniqueness [F3] identifies it as the predictor. For the pressure equation, $$ \Delta_h(k^{-1}q)=k^{-1}D_hG_hq=k^{-1}D_h\widetilde u^{n+1}; $$ both sides have mean zero and [F3] gives $\phi^{n+1}=k^{-1}q$. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

## Statement

Let $U$ be a smooth solution with values in $\mathcal G$ of the unforced balance law in [[def-compressible-navier-stokes-fourier-model]]. Then

$$\partial_t\eta(U)+\sum_{j=1}^d\partial_j\left(\eta(U)u_j+\kappa\frac{\partial_jT}{T}\right) =-\sum_{j,k=1}^d(\partial_jv)^TK_{jk}(U)(\partial_kv) =-\left(\frac{\tau:\nabla u}{T}+\frac{\kappa|\nabla T|^2}{T^2}\right)\le0.$$

This is a local smooth identity; it makes no boundary discretization claim.

## Statement

In one dimension, let $a$ be measurable, $1$-periodic, and satisfy $0<\lambda\le a\le\Lambda$. For a phase $\theta\in\mathbb R$ and ratio $r=\delta/\epsilon\ge1$, let $w_r\in V_\#$ solve $\int_0^1a(\theta+ry)(1+w_r')v'\,dy=0$ for every $v\in V_\#$, and define $A_r(\theta)=\int_0^1a(\theta+ry)(1+w_r')\,dy$. Then
$$A_r(\theta)=\left(\int_0^1\frac{dy}{a(\theta+ry)}\right)^{-1},\qquad A^*=\left(\int_0^1\frac{dy}{a(y)}\right)^{-1},$$
and
$$|A_r(\theta)-A^*|\le\frac{2\Lambda^2}{\lambda r}=\frac{2\Lambda^2}{\lambda}\frac\epsilon\delta.$$
No dimension-independent bound for the unaligned case is claimed here.

1.1 For either $b=a$ or $b(y)=a(\theta+ry)$, define $c_b=(\int_0^1b^{-1})^{-1}$ and $h_b=c_b/b-1$. The ellipticity bounds make $h_b\in L^\infty(0,1)$, and $\int_0^1h_b=0$. Thus $\chi_b(t)=\int_0^th_b(s)ds$ has equal endpoint values; its periodic extension, after subtracting its mean, belongs to $V_\#$. Since $b(1+\chi_b')=c_b$, for every periodic $v\in V_\#$ one has $\int_0^1b(1+\chi_b')v'=c_b(v(1)-v(0))=0$. It solves the cell equation. If two mean-zero solutions existed, testing their difference equation by the difference would give $\int b|\chi'-\widetilde\chi'|^2=0$, hence their difference is a mean-zero constant and is zero. This proves both harmonic-mean formulas, including the nonperiodic-in-$y$ sampled coefficient under periodic coupling. [F1, F2, F3, algebra]
cases.reason: The one-dimensional sampled cell problem has a harmonic-mean coefficient, whose incomplete-period remainder is bounded by the sampling ratio. The sampled microcell is the full unit interval and the sampling ratio is at least one, so no empty averaging window is involved.

For a phase $\theta\in\mathbb R$ and ratio $r=\delta/\epsilon\ge1$, let $w_r\in V_\#$ solve $\int_0^1a(\theta+ry)(1+w_r')v'\,dy=0$ for every $v\in V_\#$, and define $A_r(\theta)=\int_0^1a(\theta+ry)(1+w_r')\,dy$. Then
$$A_r(\theta)=\left(\int_0^1\frac{dy}{a(\theta+ry)}\right)^{-1},\qquad A^*=\left(\int_0^1\frac{dy}{a(y)}\right)^{-1},$$
and
$$|A_r(\theta)-A^*|\le\frac{2\Lambda^2}{\lambda r}=\frac{2\Lambda^2}{\lambda}\frac\epsilon\delta.$$
No dimension-independent bound for the unaligned case is claimed here.

1.1 For either $b=a$ or $b(y)=a(\theta+ry)$, define $c_b=(\int_0^1b^{-1})^{-1}$ and $h_b=c_b/b-1$. The ellipticity bounds make $h_b\in L^\infty(0,1)$, and $\int_0^1h_b=0$. Thus $\chi_b(t)=\int_0^th_b(s)ds$ has equal endpoint values; its periodic extension, after subtracting its mean, belongs to $V_\#$. Since $b(1+\chi_b')=c_b$, for every periodic $v\in V_\#$ one has $\int_0^1b(1+\chi_b')v'=c_b(v(1)-v(0))=0$. It solves the cell equation. If two mean-zero solutions existed, testing their difference equation by the difference would give $\int b|\chi'-\widetilde\chi'|^2=0$, hence their difference is a mean-zero constant and is zero. This proves both harmonic-mean formulas, including the nonperiodic-in-$y$ sampled coefficient under periodic coupling. [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 Put $g=1/a$ and $I=\int_0^1g$. Write $r=N+s$ with integer $N\ge1$ and $0\le s<1$. Periodicity gives $\int_0^r g(\theta+t)dt=NI+R,\qquad R=\int_\theta^{\theta+s}g(t)dt,$ so $\int_0^1g(\theta+ry)dy=I+(R-sI)/r$. Since $0<g\le1/\lambda$, both $R$ and $sI$ lie in $[0,s/\lambda]$, hence $|R-sI|\le s/\lambda\le1/\lambda$. In particular the weaker bound $|I_r-I|\le2/(\lambda r)$ holds. Also $I,I_r\ge1/\Lambda$. Therefore $|A_r-A^*|=\frac{|I_r-I|}{I_rI}\le\frac{2}{\lambda r}\Lambda^2,$ as claimed. [F1, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

space-time variable as $z=(t,x)$. If

principal block of $H$, then
$$a-\max_{c\in A}\left\{\sum_j(\alpha_j^c(x,t)X_{jj}+b_j^c(x,t)p_j)+f^c(x,t)\right\}\le0.$$

## Statement

Let $u_0$ be continuous and periodic, and let $B$ and $L$ bound the drift and
running cost in [[def-na-first-order-hjb-cauchy-problem]]. For the semi-Lagrangian
scheme, if $t_n=n\tau\to0$, $h_{\max}\to0$, and
$h_{\max}^2/\tau\to0$, then
$$\sup_i|U_i^n-u_0(x_i)|\longrightarrow0.$$
For the upwind scheme, the same conclusion holds when $t_n\to0$,
$h_{\max}\to0$, and its CFL condition holds. Both statements are uniform over
all finite control policies and remain true for a finite control discretization.

1.1 For a semi-Lagrangian row at a node $x_i$ and action $a$, view its interpolation weights as a finite probability vector on the cell nodes around $y=x_i+\tau b_a(x_i,t)$. In a periodic lift, the weighted mean of each coordinate is $(1-\theta_j)x_{i_j}+\theta_j(x_{i_j}+h_j)=y_j$, by the product formula in [F1]. The centered interpolation error $\xi$ therefore has weighted mean zero and satisfies $|\xi|^2\le\sum_jh_j^2$. [F1, given, algebra]

1.2 For an upwind row, the weights in [F2] are nonnegative and sum to one by CFL. The weighted mean displacement to the previous-time node is $\tau b_a$: in coordinate $j$ it is $\tau(b_j^+/h_j)h_j-\tau(b_j^-/h_j)h_j=\tau b_j$. Its centered error $\xi$ has mean zero and second moment at most $\tau\sum_j|b_j|h_j\le\tau B\sum_jh_j$, since subtracting the squared mean cannot increase the second moment. [F2, given, algebra]
cases.evidence: Finite weighted control paths bound small-time displacement and reward, proving a uniform discrete initial trace. At time index zero the path has no increments or rewards and the initialization is exactly the supplied initial datum.

## Statement

Let $u_0$ be continuous and periodic, and let $B$ and $L$ bound the drift and
running cost in [[def-na-first-order-hjb-cauchy-problem]]. For the semi-Lagrangian
scheme, if $t_n=n\tau\to0$, $h_{\max}\to0$, and

The weighted mean displacement to the previous-time node is $\tau b_a$: in coordinate $j$ it is $\tau(b_j^+/h_j)h_j-\tau(b_j^-/h_j)h_j=\tau b_j$. Its centered error $\xi$ has mean zero and second moment at most $\tau\sum_j|b_j|h_j\le\tau B\sum_jh_j$, since subtracting the squared mean cannot increase the second moment. [F2, given, algebra]

1.3 Unroll either update for the finite number $n$ of steps. At each stage the minimum chooses one of finitely many control rows, and each row is a finite weighted average; induction therefore represents the value as the minimum of finite weighted path costs $u_0(X_n)+\sum_{r<n}\tau\ell_r$. Along any such controlled path the sum of the drift increments has norm at most $Bt$. The centered increments have conditional mean zero. For $r<s$, summing the increment $\xi_s$ over all next-branch weights from each fixed path prefix through time $s-1$ gives zero; hence the finite weighted cross term $\mathbb E(\xi_r\cdot\xi_s)$ is zero. Expanding the square therefore shows that their total second moment is at most $n\sum_jh_j^2$ for the semi-Lagrangian rows and $tB\sum_jh_j$ for the upwind rows. Thus the endpoint displacement obeys $$\mathbb E|X_n-x_i|^2\le2B^2t^2+2n\sum_jh_j^2$$ for the semi-Lagrangian case and $$\mathbb E|X_n-x_i|^2\le2B^2t^2+2tB\sum_jh_j$$ for the upwind case. Every path's accumulated reward has magnitude at most $Lt$. [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the input hypotheses of [[alg-nufft-certified-gaussian-gridding-type1-type2]]. If $N=0$, the type-1 output is exactly zero and the type-2 output is empty, so their coordinatewise errors are zero. For $N>0$, fix a successful candidate with $P=\prod_rM_r$, exact multipliers $d_k=\prod_r\sqrt{\tau_r}\exp(-\pi\tau_rk_r^2)$, $d_{\min}=\prod_r\sqrt{\tau_r}\exp(-\pi\tau_rK_r^2)>0$, $s_r=\exp(-\pi\tau_rM_r(M_r-2K_r))$, and the exact spread-tail quantity $T_d$ of [[lem-nufft-gaussian-spread-truncation-tail]]. Put
$$\alpha=\prod_{r=1}^d\left(1+\frac{2s_r}{1-s_r}\right)-1,\qquad \epsilon_0=\alpha+\frac{T_d}{P d_{\min}}.$$
The algorithm returns an outward upper bound $\epsilon_{\rm ana}\ge\epsilon_0$.

For a type-1 output center array $\widehat F$ and its returned finite-arithmetic radius $B_{\rm round}$,
$$\|\widehat F-F\|_\infty\le\epsilon_{\rm ana}\|c\|_1+B_{\rm round}.$$
For the type-2 output center array $\widehat g$ and its returned radius $B_{\rm round}^*$,
$$\|\widehat g-A^*f\|_\infty\le\epsilon_{\rm ana}\|f\|_1+B_{\rm round}^*,$$
where $A_{k,j}=e^{-2\pi i k\cdot x_j}$ is the exact type-1 matrix and $A^*$ is its conjugate transpose.
When $N=0$, the type-2 output is empty and its coordinatewise assertion is vacuous; the procedure returns zero radius for this empty-output branch.

For fixed $d$, widths $w_r\le w$, image cutoffs $L_r\le L$, and fixed interval-series controls, one candidate's scalar grid/FFT/deconvolution work is
$$O\!\left(P\log P+N\prod_{r=1}^d(2w_r+1)\sum_{r=1}^d(2L_r+1)+|\mathcal K|\right).$$
Thus for bounded $w,L$ it is $O(P\log P+Nw^d)$, apart from the explicitly counted finite elementary-range evaluation work. No type-3 fast-cost claim follows.

1.1 If $N=0$, [F17] and the finite sums in [F1] give exact zero type-1 output and an empty type-2 output; [F12] assigns zero to empty norms, so both error assertions hold with zero radii. For the remaining proof assume $N>0$. Let $S_\infty$ be the full spread matrix with entries $(S_\infty)_{\ell j}=\Phi_\tau(\ell_1/M_1-x_{j,1},\ldots,\ell_d/M_d-x_{j,d})$, and let $S$ keep only the entries in each source's product neighborhood. Define the mode-by-grid matrix $Q_{k\ell}=P^{-1}e^{-2\pi i\sum_rk_r\ell_r/M_r}$ and the diagonal mode matrix $D_{kk}=d_k$, with $D^{-1}_{kk}=1/d_k$ by the positive-multiplier premise. The products below use the finite matrix multiplication of [F19]. The normalized grid sum in [F2], applied to the unit source vector $e_j$, says that every entry of $D^{-1}QS_\infty-A$ has modulus at most $\alpha$. For each column $j$, [F3] bounds the sum of the nonnegative deleted entries by $T_d$; since $|Q_{k\ell}|=P^{-1}$, it follows that $|(Q(S_\infty-S))_{kj}|\le T_d/P$. By [F10], $|k_r|\le K_r$, and [F14]–[F15], $d_k\ge d_{\min}>0$, so $|(D^{-1}Q(S_\infty-S))_{kj}|\le T_d/(P d_{\min})$. Adding the two matrix differences gives $|(D^{-1}QS-A)_{kj}|\le\epsilon_0$ for every $k,j$. For each row, multiplication by $c$ and the complex modulus laws [F21] give $|((D^{-1}QS-A)c)_k|\le\epsilon_0\sum_j|c_j|$, hence $\|(D^{-1}QS-A)c\|_\infty\le\epsilon_0\|c\|_1$ by [F12]. Finally [F9] gives $\epsilon_0\le\epsilon_{\rm ana}$ for the returned outward bound. [A1, F1, F2, F3, F9, F10, F12, F14, F15, F17, F19, F21, F22, algebra]

3.2 The type-2 exact finite matrix computed by the algorithm is $\widetilde A^*$. By [F19], $(\widetilde A)_{kj}=d_k^{-1}\sum_\ell Q_{k\ell}S_{\ell j}$. Since $d_k$ and $S_{\ell j}$ are real by [F14]–[F15] and [F20], conjugating this entry gives $d_k^{-1}\sum_\ell\overline{Q_{k\ell}}S_{\ell j}$; this is exactly the $(j,k)$ entry of $S^*Q^*D^{-1}$ by the same finite-product formula. In the slot notation of step 2.1, $Q^*=P^{-1/2}U_P^*R_\kappa^*$, where $R_\kappa^*$ embeds a mode vector into the grid slots $\kappa(k)$ and zero-fills every other slot; this is the inverse-FFT construction in step 4. Thus $\widetilde A^*=S^*Q^*D^{-1}$. Step 1.1 gives $|(\widetilde A-A)_{kj}|\le\epsilon_0$ for each entry, so the complex modulus laws [F21] give $|((\widetilde A^*-A^*)f)_j|\le\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}|(\widetilde A-A)_{kj}|\,|f_k|\le\epsilon_0\|f\|_1.$ It remains to bound the finite-arithmetic discrepancy. ## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the input hypotheses of [[alg-nufft-certified-gaussian-gridding-type1-type2]]. If $N=0$, the type-1 output is exactly zero and the type-2 output is empty, so their coordinatewise errors are zero. Put
$$\alpha=\prod_{r=1}^d\left(1+\frac{2s_r}{1-s_r}\right)-1,\qquad \epsilon_0=\alpha+\frac{T_d}{P d_{\min}}.$$
The algorithm returns an outward upper bound $\epsilon_{\rm ana}\ge\epsilon_0$.

For a type-1 output center array $\widehat F$ and its returned finite-arithmetic radius $B_{\rm round}$,
$$\|\widehat F-F\|_\infty\le\epsilon_{\rm ana}\|c\|_1+B_{\rm round}.$$
For the type-2 output center array $\widehat g$ and its returned radius $B_{\rm round}^*$,
$$\|\widehat g-A^*f\|_\infty\le\epsilon_{\rm ana}\|f\|_1+B_{\rm round}^*,$$
where $A_{k,j}=e^{-2\pi i k\cdot x_j}$ is the exact type-1 matrix and $A^*$ is its conjugate transpose.
When $N=0$, the type-2 output is empty and its coordinatewise assertion is vacuous; the procedure returns zero radius for this empty-output branch.

For fixed $d$, widths $w_r\le w$, image cutoffs $L_r\le L$, and fixed interval-series controls, one candidate's scalar grid/FFT/deconvolution work is
$$O\!\left(P\log P+N\prod_{r=1}^d(2w_r+1)\sum_{r=1}^d(2L_r+1)+|\mathcal K|\right).$$
Thus for bounded $w,L$ it is $O(P\log P+Nw^d)$, apart from the explicitly counted finite elementary-range evaluation work. No type-3 fast-cost claim follows.

1.1 If $N=0$, [F17] and the finite sums in [F1] give exact zero type-1 output and an empty type-2 output; [F12] assigns zero to empty norms, so both error assertions hold with zero radii. For the remaining proof assume $N>0$. Let $S_\infty$ be the full spread matrix with entries $(S_\infty)_{\ell j}=\Phi_\tau(\ell_1/M_1-x_{j,1},\ldots,\ell_d/M_d-x_{j,d})$, and let $S$ keep only the entries in each source's product neighborhood. Define the mode-by-grid matrix $Q_{k\ell}=P^{-1}e^{-2\pi i\sum_rk_r\ell_r/M_r}$ and the diagonal mode matrix $D_{kk}=d_k$, with $D^{-1}_{kk}=1/d_k$ by the positive-multiplier premise. The products below use the finite matrix multiplication of [F19]. The normalized grid sum in [F2], applied to the unit source vector $e_j$, says that every entry of $D^{-1}QS_\infty-A$ has modulus at most $\alpha$. For each column $j$, [F3] bounds the sum of the nonnegative deleted entries by $T_d$; since $|Q_{k\ell}|=P^{-1}$, it follows that $|(Q(S_\infty-S))_{kj}|\le T_d/P$. By [F10], $|k_r|\le K_r$, and [F14]–[F15], $d_k\ge d_{\min}>0$, so $|(D^{-1}Q(S_\infty-S))_{kj}|\le T_d/(P d_{\min})$. Adding the two matrix differences gives $|(D^{-1}QS-A)_{kj}|\le\epsilon_0$ for every $k,j$. For each row, multiplication by $c$ and the complex modulus laws [F21] give $|((D^{-1}QS-A)c)_k|\le\epsilon_0\sum_j|c_j|$, hence $\|(D^{-1}QS-A)c\|_\infty\le\epsilon_0\|c\|_1$ by [F12]. 2.1 Let $g=Sc$ be the exact truncated spread and $u$ the dyadic center grid computed by the algorithm. The finite image sums and symmetric remainder intervals enclose every exact kernel by [F4]; isotonicity of the outward DAG operations then gives $\|g-u\|_2\le E_{\rm eval}$, with norms as in [F12]. By [F18], the counting Euclidean norm has the triangle inequality. For coordinate axis $r$, regard its $P/M_r$ length-$M_r$ FFTs as one block-diagonal operator. Squaring and summing the linewise supplier bound [F5] gives a normwise error at most $\rho_r$ times the block input norm; the exact block transform is unitary by [F6]. If $x_r$ and $y_r$ are the computed and exact outputs after axes $1,\ldots,r$, the triangle inequality [F18], the local error bound and unitarity give $\|x_r\|_2\le(1+\rho_r)\|x_{r-1}\|_2$ and $\|x_r-y_r\|_2\le\|x_{r-1}-y_{r-1}\|_2+\rho_r\|x_{r-1}\|_2$. For each extracted coordinate, the FFT discrepancy has modulus at most $\rho U$, since a coordinate modulus is bounded by the Euclidean norm. The exact scaling by $P^{-1/2}$ and exact division by the mode multiplier therefore make its deconvolved discrepancy at most $\rho U/(\sqrt P\,d_k)\le\rho U/(\sqrt P\,d_{\min}^-)$, using [F15] and $0<d_{\min}^-\le d_{\min}\le d_k$. By [F4], the computed scaling/deconvolution rectangle encloses the exact scaling/deconvolution of the computed FFT coordinate, so its distance from the returned lower-left center is at most $b_k$. The algorithm forms $R_{\rm FFT}$ outward from the actual input norm bound and the verified call factors; [F7] and the complex triangle inequality [F21] then give distance at most $b_k+R_{\rm FFT}\le r_k$ from that center to the exact deconvolution of the dyadic center grid. This justifies the full containment claimed in [F7], including the previously omitted computed FFT error. To transfer the grid-center enclosure, define $U_P$ as the exact unitary DFT on the full rectangular grid and $R_\kappa$ as restriction to the slots $\kappa(k)$. Since $M_r>2K_r$, two modes in $[-K_r,K_r]$ with the same residue differ by a multiple of $M_r$ of magnitude less than $M_r$, hence are equal; coordinatewise, $\kappa$ is injective. The grid transform in step 1.1 is $Q=P^{-1/2}R_\kappa U_P$. For any finite array $z$, each $|z_k|^2$ is a nonnegative summand of $\sum_\ell|z_\ell|^2$, so [F12] and [F23] give $\|z\|_\infty\le\|z\|_2$. Thus the additional deconvolution error is at most $E_{\rm eval}/(\sqrt P d_{\min})$. The algorithm defines $B_{\rm round}=\max_k r_k+E_{\rm eval}/(\sqrt P d_{\min}^-)$; using $d_{\min}^-\le d_{\min}$, taking the maximum returned $r_k$ and adding its grid-center term gives the asserted radius. [F4, F5, F6, F7, F9, F10, F12, F14, F15, F18, F21, F23, step 1.1, algebra]

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and a neutral finite point-source configuration on
$A\mathbb Z^3$ from [[def-ewald-three-dimensional-periodic-source-data]]. Fix
$\alpha>0$, real and reciprocal cutoffs $R,K_c\ge1$, a mesh with integers
$M_r\ge1$ and order $P\ge2$, and a finite symmetric retained set
$\mathcal K\subseteq\{k\in\mathbb Z^3\setminus\{0\}:|\kappa_k|\le K_c\}$
that is injective modulo $(M_1,M_2,M_3)$ and has $|k_r|<M_r/2$ and $D(k)\ne0$
for every $k\in\mathcal K$. Put $Q=\sum_i|q_i|$ and let
$$\mathcal B_{K_c}=\{k\in\mathbb Z^3\setminus\{0\}:|\kappa_k|\le K_c\},\qquad \mathcal M_{K_c}=\mathcal B_{K_c}\setminus\mathcal K.$$
This in-ball omitted set is finite. Write $M_R=\lfloor R\rfloor$,
$M_K=\lfloor K_c\rfloor$, $C_R=C_A$, and $C_K=C_{2\pi A^{-T}}$ for the shell
constants in [[lem-ewald-lattice-shell-gaussian-tail-controllers]]. Choose
integers $J_R\ge M_R$, $J_K\ge M_K$ such that
$2\alpha^2J_R(J_R+1)\ge3$ and
$\frac{1}{2\alpha^2}J_K(J_K+1)\ge3$. Let $U_3(\beta,M,J)$ be that supplier's
finite upper controller for $\sum_{m=M}^\infty(m+1)^3e^{-\beta m^2}$, and put
$$\begin{aligned} \overline B_R^U&=\frac{QC_R}{\sqrt\pi\alpha}U_3(\alpha^2,M_R,J_R),& \overline B_R^E&=\frac{Q^2C_R}{2\sqrt\pi\alpha}U_3(\alpha^2,M_R,J_R),& \overline B_R^{F,i}&=\frac{|q_i|QC_R}{\sqrt\pi}(2\alpha+\alpha^{-1})U_3(\alpha^2,M_R,J_R),\\ \overline B_K^U&=\frac{4\pi QC_K}{V}U_3((4\alpha^2)^{-1},M_K,J_K),& \overline B_K^E&=\frac{2\pi Q^2C_K}{V}U_3((4\alpha^2)^{-1},M_K,J_K),& \overline B_K^{F,i}&=\frac{4\pi|q_i|QC_K}{V}U_3((4\alpha^2)^{-1},M_K,J_K). \end{aligned}$$

For $\phi_s(r)=\operatorname{erfc}(\alpha r)/r$, define the finite real-space
potential at an off-source point by
$$S_R(x)=\sum_iq_i\sum_{\substack{\lambda\in\Lambda\\|x-x_i+\lambda|\le R}}\phi_s(|x-x_i+\lambda|),$$
and the finite real energy by
$$E_R=\frac12\sum_i\sum_j\sum_{\substack{\lambda\in\Lambda\\|x_i-x_j+\lambda|\le R}}'q_iq_j\phi_s(|x_i-x_j+\lambda|),$$
where the prime omits exactly $(j,\lambda)=(i,0)$. Let
$$F_{R,i}=-q_i\sum_{\substack{1\le j\le n,\ \lambda\in\Lambda\\(j,\lambda)\ne(i,0),\,|x_i-x_j+\lambda|\le R}}q_j\,\phi_s'(|x_i-x_j+\lambda|)\frac{x_i-x_j+\lambda}{|x_i-x_j+\lambda|}.$$
The cutoff index set is held fixed in this force sum; the cutoff indicator is
not differentiated. Set
$$\widetilde U(x)=S_R(x)+U_{M,\mathcal K}(x),$$
$$\widetilde E^\chi=E_R+E_{M,\mathcal K}^\chi-\frac{\alpha}{\sqrt\pi}\sum_iq_i^2,\qquad \widetilde F_i^\chi=F_{R,i}+F_{M,i}^\chi,$$
where $\chi=\mathrm{uncorr}$ uses the uncorrected energy and force of
[[thm-ewald-pme-reciprocal-energy-force-error-bound]], and $\chi=\mathrm{corr}$ uses
its optional diagonal self-corrected branch. For the uncorrected branch suppose
the derivative/gather residuals are $H_k$; the corrected branch uses the
energy-gradient gather, so $H_k=0$.

Suppose the computed finite outputs $\widehat U(x),\widehat E^\chi,\widehat
F_i^\chi$ have certified arithmetic radii $\varepsilon_U,\varepsilon_E,
\varepsilon_{F,i}\ge0$ relative to $\widetilde U,\widetilde E^\chi,
\widetilde F_i^\chi$, respectively. Define
$$\begin{aligned} \eta_U={}&\overline B_R^U+\overline B_K^U+Q\sum_{m\in\mathcal M_{K_c}}c_m+Q\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_kA_k(2+A_k)+\varepsilon_U,\\ \eta_E^{\mathrm{uncorr}}={}&\overline B_R^E+\overline B_K^E+\frac{Q^2}{2}\sum_{m\in\mathcal M_{K_c}}c_m+\frac{Q^2}{2}\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_kA_k(2+A_k)+\varepsilon_E,\\ \eta_E^{\mathrm{corr}}={}&\overline B_R^E+\overline B_K^E+\frac{Q^2}{2}\sum_{m\in\mathcal M_{K_c}}c_m+\frac{Q^2-\sum_iq_i^2}{2}\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_kA_k(2+A_k)+\varepsilon_E,\\ \eta_{F,i}^{\mathrm{uncorr}}={}&\overline B_R^{F,i}+\overline B_K^{F,i}+|q_i|Q\sum_{m\in\mathcal M_{K_c}}c_m|\kappa_m|+|q_i|Q\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k[|\kappa_k|A_k+(1+A_k)B_k+(1+A_k)H_k]+\varepsilon_{F,i},\\ \eta_{F,i}^{\mathrm{corr}}={}&\overline B_R^{F,i}+\overline B_K^{F,i}+|q_i|Q\sum_{m\in\mathcal M_{K_c}}c_m|\kappa_m|+|q_i|(Q-|q_i|)\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k[|\kappa_k|A_k+(1+A_k)B_k]+\varepsilon_{F,i}. \end{aligned}$$
Then, for every off-source $x$ and each particle $i$,
$$|\widehat U(x)-U_\alpha(x)|\le\eta_U,\qquad |\widehat E^\chi-E|\le\eta_E^\chi,\qquad \|\widehat F_i^\chi-F_i\|_2\le\eta_{F,i}^\chi.$$
Here $U_\alpha,E,F_i$ are the exact mean-zero periodic Ewald potential,
renormalized energy, and particle force. The finite omitted-mode sums
$\mathcal M_{K_c}$ explicitly charge every mode in the radial ball that the
mesh did not retain, including Nyquist modes. Missing arithmetic radii do not
produce a certificate; no RMS estimate is substituted for these deterministic
bounds.

For the formal exact-constant work count, let $\mathsf N_{\mathrm{img}}$ be
the total number of candidate real-image indices inspected in the finite
potential, energy, and force loops, and let $\mathsf N_{\mathrm{cert}}$ be the
total number of mode and finite controller entries inspected in constructing
the omitted-mode ledger and error certificate. Count each such outer-loop
inspection as one work unit and count the transform arithmetic in the formal
exact-constant model of [[thm-na-arbitrary-length-fft-correctness-and-cost]].
For fixed $P$, the finite evaluation uses
$$O\!\left(N_g\log(2N_g)+nP^3+\mathsf N_{\mathrm{img}}+\mathsf N_{\mathrm{cert}}\right)$$
work units, with at most three tensor transforms before optional
mesh-self correction. The correction adds
$$O\!\left(N_g\log(2N_g)+nP^6\right)$$
when its cyclic kernel is precomputed. These counts do not include interval
precision, elementary-function evaluation, memory traffic, bit complexity, or
the transform subroutine's integer factor search and phase evaluation; no
operation count is used as an accuracy bound.

2.1 The exact Ewald series is the sum of the full real-space term, all retained reciprocal modes, all in-ball omitted reciprocal modes, and the reciprocal tail beyond $K_c$, with the exact self constant in the energy. The finite approximations include the real terms through $R$, the selected mesh approximation on $\mathcal K$, and that same self constant. Thus their exact-real differences split into the real cutoff tail, the reciprocal shell tail, the finite omitted in-ball terms, and the retained mesh alias/differentiation error. Step 1.2 bounds the real and reciprocal cutoff tails, step 1.3 accounts for every omitted in-ball mode, and step 1.4 bounds the retained mesh error. By [F3], [F4], and the triangle inequality, the absolute values or norms of these parts sum to the first terms displayed in each $\eta$. [A1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 1.4, algebra]

4.1 For fixed $P\ge2$, the finite support enclosure gives at most $P+2\le2P$ candidates per coordinate. Thus each particle's spread and potential/force gathers use $O(P^3)$ support tuples; grid initialization costs $O(N_g)$ and is absorbed by the transform count. A tensor transform along coordinate $r$ consists of $N_g/M_r$ one-dimensional transforms of length $M_r$. By [F8] this costs $O(N_g\log(2M_r))$, and summing over the three coordinates gives $O(N_g\log(2N_g))$. The uncorrected computation uses one forward transform and at most two inverse/gather transforms. The finite real-image and mode/controller loops contribute $\mathsf N_{\mathrm{img}}+\mathsf N_{\mathrm{cert}}$ by definition, proving the stated total count. The optional correction adds one transform to form its cyclic kernel and at most $(P+2)^6=O(P^6)$ support-pair products per particle, which gives its stated cost. The arithmetic radii are certified separately and do not follow from this operation count. [F8, algebra] ∎

## Example

The scalar transfer function $H(z)=C(zI-A)^{-1}B$ with $A=[2]$ and
$B=C=[1]$ is $H(z)=1/(z-2)$. On the ordered sample set
$Z=(0,1,3,4)$, exact AAA with support budget $B_{\max}=2$, tolerance $0$,
and bidiagonal-QR sweep budget $S=1$ selects support nodes $1$ and $3$ and
returns the exact transfer function. Its reduced denominator has the true
pole $z=2$.

1.1 The data in order are $(-1/2,-1,1,1/2)$, with mean zero. Thus $\eta_0=1>\tau=0$, so the initial tolerance test does not return. Their largest absolute residuals are tied at $z=1$ and $z=3$; [F1] selects the earlier sample $z=1$. The first Loewner matrix is the single column $(-1/2,1,1/2)^T$, since its entries are $$\frac{H(0)-H(1)}{0-1}=-\frac12,\qquad \frac{H(3)-H(1)}{3-1}=1,\qquad \frac{H(4)-H(1)}{4-1}=\frac12.$$ Since its right domain is one-dimensional, the selected unit weight is $1$ under the phase rule. Its Householder reduction has a single diagonal entry; by [F5] there is only a singleton block, so the SVD call converges without using a sweep. The one-support quotient is the constant $-1$. Its remaining residual magnitudes are $1/2,2,3/2$ at $z=0,3,4$, respectively, so $\eta_1=2>\tau$ and the second support is $z=3$. [given, F1, F4, F5, F7, algebra]

1.2 The remaining sample points are $0$ and $4$. In that row and support order, the Loewner matrix is $$L=\begin{bmatrix}-1/2&1/2\\1/2&-1/2\end{bmatrix}.$$ The rows are negatives of one another and $L(1,1)^T=0$, so $L$ has rank one, its smallest singular value is zero, and its right nullspace is spanned by $(1,1)$. The orthogonal projection of $e_1$ onto this line is $(1/2,1/2)$; normalizing it and applying the positive-real phase rule [F1] gives $w=(1,1)/\sqrt2$, whose components are both nonzero. [given, F1, algebra]

## Statement

Fix a finite Hermitian Hamiltonian $H$ on the coefficient space of the states. Consider an infinite sequence obtained by repeatedly applying one full no-truncation sweep of [[alg-na-alternating-tensor-optimization-and-effective-eigenproblems]], starting from a supplied concrete open-boundary TT core list or periodic trace presentation representing a normalized state, with fixed bond dimensions and a fixed finite list of one-site or two-site update windows. Assume the canonical core arrays at every stage of each sweep are bounded and converge componentwise in one consistent gauge to a single normalized canonical core tuple. Then the limit is **coordinatewise stationary**, meaning that for each update window, its limiting center vector minimizes the Rayleigh quotient of the effective Hermitian Hamiltonian over all unit center vectors with the other limiting cores fixed. In particular, each limiting center is a lowest eigenvector of its limiting effective Hamiltonian. This is conditional on the stated convergence; it asserts neither convergence of DMRG nor global minimality.

1.1 Fix one update window. Each entry of its prefix and suffix interface and of its effective Hamiltonian is a finite sum of products of core entries and fixed entries of $H$. Therefore these entries depend continuously on the canonical core arrays. By the assumed componentwise convergence at every stage, the center vectors and effective Hamiltonians at this window converge to limits $x_*$ and $H_{\mathrm{eff},*}$. [given, F1, F2, algebra]
cases.evidence: Convergence of every canonical update stage lets exact local Rayleigh minimization pass to each fixed update window of the limiting tensor presentation. Both open-boundary cores and periodic trace presentations are expressly allowed, but all center spaces and update-window dimensions stay fixed during the limit.

## Statement

Fix $x>0$, integers $N\ge1$ and $0\le n<N$, and define the exact backward
recurrence solution by $u_{N+1}=0$, $u_N=1$, and
$u_{j-1}=2ju_j/x-u_{j+1}$ for $j=N,N-1,\ldots,1$. If
$D_{N+1}(x)\ne0$, put $q=-J_{N+1}(x)/D_{N+1}(x)$. For $s\in\{0,1\}$ such
that $J_s(x)+qD_s(x)\ne0$, let
$\widehat J_n=J_s(x)u_n/u_s$. Then

$$\widehat J_n-J_n= \frac{q\bigl(J_sD_n-J_nD_s\bigr)}{J_s+qD_s}.$$

This is a finite-$N$ identity. It makes no assertion that the error tends to
zero as $N\to\infty$.

1.1 The sequence $J+qD$ obeys the recurrence by [F2] and [F3], and its value at $N+1$ is $J_{N+1}+qD_{N+1}=0$. Its value at $N$ is nonzero: if it too were zero, backward recurrence would make it zero at every index, contradicting the linear independence in [F1] and its coefficient $1$ on $J$. Therefore $(J+qD)/(J_N+qD_N)$ has the terminal values $u_{N+1}=0,u_N=1$. Uniqueness of the finite backward recurrence gives $u_j=(J_j+qD_j)/(J_N+qD_N)$ for $0\le j\le N$. [given, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 Taking the ratio of the formulas for $j=n$ and $j=s$ yields $u_n/u_s=(J_n+qD_n)/(J_s+qD_s)$. Since the denominator is nonzero, $$\widehat J_n-J_n =J_s\frac{J_n+qD_n}{J_s+qD_s}-J_n =\frac{q(J_sD_n-J_nD_s)}{J_s+qD_s}.$$ Every equality uses this single fixed terminal index $N$; no limit in $N$ was taken. [given, step 1.1, algebra] ∎
cases.evidence: A finite backward Miller solution is a normalized combination of two recurrence solutions, yielding an exact terminal-error identity. The terminal value at the next index is exactly zero, but both the complementary terminal denominator and the selected normalization denominator are required nonzero.

## Example

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, and also assume Dependent Choice $\mathrm{DC}$ if $u_0\in L^1(\mathbb R)$. Let $f_B(s)=s^2/2$ and use the Godunov flux $G$ of
[[def-godunov-flux-for-burgers]]. For every compact invariant interval $I\subseteq[-M,M]$
with $M>0$, the two coordinate Lipschitz bounds can be taken to be
$L_1=L_2=M$, and $G$ is nondecreasing in its first argument and nonincreasing
in its second. Therefore, for any $u_0\in\mathrm{BV}_b(\mathbb R)$ with values
in $I$, every mesh family satisfying
$$\frac{\tau_m}{h_m}\le\frac1{2M},\qquad \frac{\tau_m}{h_m}\ge c_*>0,\qquad h_m,\tau_m\to0$$
falls under [[thm-monotone-finite-volume-entropy-convergence]] and converges
strongly locally to the unique Burgers entropy solution.

1.2 Fix $a\in[-M,M]$. On the branches of [F1], $b\mapsto G(a,b)$ is either constant, $b^2/2$ for $b\le0$, or $\max\{a^2,b^2\}/2$ on $b<a$. As $b$ increases, $b^2/2$ decreases on the negative axis; on $b<a$, the maximum decreases while $|b|>|a|$ and is constant after $|b|\le|a|$; the remaining $a\le b$ branches are constant or decrease to zero. Boundary values agree by [F2]. Hence $G(a,\cdot)$ is nonincreasing. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.3 On every smooth branch the derivative in the varying coordinate has absolute value at most $R$ on $[-R,R]^2$. The maximum branch has the same bound because $\max\{a^2,b^2\}/2$ is piecewise one of the two square branches. The finite branch partition and continuity from [F2] therefore give coordinate Lipschitz bounds $R$ on every compact square $[-R,R]^2$, proving that $G$ is locally Lipschitz on $\mathbb R^2$. Applying the same estimate with $R=M$ gives coordinate Lipschitz bounds $L_1=L_2=M$ on the target square. Consistency is [F2], so the full CFL bound is $\lambda(L_1+L_2)=2M\lambda\le1$. [F1, F2, algebra]

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the Poisson/Nitsche setup of [[def-nitsche-boundary-penalty-forms]] on a connected bounded polyhedral $\Omega$. Let $u\in H^{1+r}(\Omega)$, $r>1/2$, solve $-\Delta u=f\in L^2(\Omega)$ with Dirichlet trace $g$, and let $u_h^\theta$ solve the discrete problem for $\theta\in\{0,1\}$. Use the comparison seminorm $\|\cdot\|_{\#,h}$ of the definition. Put $C_\partial$ as in [[lem-nitsche-global-boundary-flux-bound]], and assume
$$\gamma_0>(1+\theta)^2C_\partial^2/4.$$
The discrete solution exists uniquely, and
$$\|u-u_h^\theta\|_{\#,h}\le C_\theta\inf_{v_h\in V_h}\|u-v_h\|_{\#,h},\qquad C_\theta:=1+\frac{(2+\theta C_\partial+\gamma_0)(1+C_\partial^2)}{\lambda_\theta},$$
where $\lambda_\theta$ is the positive coercivity constant in [[lem-nitsche-penalty-coercivity]]. If, in addition, the Nitsche comparison-norm approximation bound [A2] holds with exponent $t>0$, then
$$\|u-u_h^\theta\|_{\#,h}\le C_\theta C_I\left(\sum_{K\in\mathcal T_h}h_K^{2t}\|u\|_{H^{1+t}(K)}^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
The result keeps the weak Dirichlet trace unconstrained in $V_h$.

1.1 The coercivity threshold in the Statement and [F3] give $a_h^	heta(v_h,v_h)\ge\lambda_	heta\|v_h\|_{E,h}^2$ for all $v_h\in V_h$. If $\|v_h\|_{E,h}=0$, then the weak gradient of $v_h$ is zero. For any ball $B$ with $\overline B\subset\Omega$, choose a slightly larger ball $B'$ still compactly contained in $\Omega$ and a smooth cutoff $\chi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ equal to one on a neighborhood of $\overline{B'}$, using [F5]. The product $\chi v_h$ lies in $H^1(\Omega)$ with compact support by [F5]; let $V$ be its zero extension to $\mathbb R^d$. On a neighborhood of $\overline{B'}$, $
abla V=
abla v_h=0$. For sufficiently small $\varepsilon$, [F5] says $V_\varepsilon=ho_\varepsilon*V$ is smooth and has gradient $ho_\varepsilon*
abla V=0$ on $B$, so it is constant there. The rescaled kernels are an $L^1$ approximate identity, and [F5] gives $V_\varepsilon	o V=v_h$ in $L^2(B)$; because $B$ has positive measure, the constants $V_\varepsilon|_B$ are Cauchy and $v_h$ is a.e. constant on $B$. The points polygonally reachable from a fixed point form a nonempty open and relatively closed subset of connected $\Omega$: if a point of $\Omega$ is in the relative closure, a small ball in $\Omega$ meets the reachable set and its line segment reaches the point. Hence any two points are joined by a polygonal path. A compact polygonal path is covered by a finite chain of overlapping interior balls, so the local constants agree. Thus every point has a neighborhood on which $v_h$ equals the same constant $c$ almost everywhere; second countability gives a countable subcover of $\Omega$, and the union of its null exceptional sets is null. On each cell its polynomial agrees a.e. with $c$ on the cell interior and therefore equals $c$ everywhere on the cell; its boundary trace is $c$. The global flux-bound supplier [F2] guarantees a boundary facet; that facet has positive measure and $h_F>0$, so the zero boundary term in $\|v_h\|_{E,h}$ forces $c=0$. Thus the energy seminorm is a norm on $V_h$. [F2, F3, F5, given, algebra]

2.1 Define the linear map $A_h:V_h\to V_h^*$ by $(A_hv_h)(w_h)=a_h^\theta(v_h,w_h)$. If $A_hv_h=0$, testing with $v_h$ and using [F3] gives $\lambda_\theta\|v_h\|_{E,h}^2\le0$, hence $v_h=0$ by step 1.1. Therefore $A_h$ is injective; since $V_h$ and its dual are finite-dimensional with equal dimension, $A_h$ is bijective. The load $\ell_h^\theta$ is a finite linear functional on $V_h$, so the discrete equation has a unique solution. [F3, step 1.1, given, algebra]

Let $A\in\mathbb F^{n\times n}$ be invertible over $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, $n\ge1$, and let $A=LU$ be an exact block lower-upper factorization. Suppose [[alg-hlr-compress-exact-lu-factors]] returns $\widehat L,\widehat U$ and exact local discarded-tail errors $e_b^L,e_c^U$. All operations and norms in this theorem are exact. Put $\epsilon_L=(\sum_b(e_b^L)^2)^{1/2}$, $\epsilon_U=(\sum_c(e_c^U)^2)^{1/2}$, $\widehat A=\widehat L\widehat U$, and $\eta=\epsilon_L\|U\|_F+\|\widehat L\|_F\epsilon_U$. Then

$$\|A-\widehat A\|_F\le\eta\qquad\text{and}\qquad\|A-\widehat A\|_2\le\eta.$$

If $q=\|A^{-1}\|_2\eta<1$, then $\widehat A$ is invertible and

$$\|\widehat A^{-1}-A^{-1}\|_2\le\frac{\|A^{-1}\|_2^2\eta}{1-q}.$$

3.1 For any matrix $R$, [F7] gives $\|R\|_2=\sigma_1(R)$, while [F8] at rank cap zero gives $\|R\|_F=(\sum_j\sigma_j(R)^2)^{1/2}$. Hence $\|R\|_2\le\|R\|_F$. Applying this to $R=A-\widehat A$ and using step 2.1 proves $\|A-\widehat A\|_2\le\eta$. [F7, F8, step 2.1, algebra]

## Example

Let $N=2M$ with $M\ge2$ on the uniform fine P1 Dirichlet mesh of $(0,1)$.
Take the coarse P1 space on the even nodes and one local space
$\operatorname{span}\{\phi_{2k-1}\}$ for each odd node. The exact two-level
additive Schwarz operator has $C_0\le2$, $C_1\le2$, and hence
$\kappa_A(BA)\le4$, independently of $M$.

1.2 On each fine interval, at most one odd nodal hat has nonzero derivative. Thus only the coarse derivative and at most one local derivative can be nonzero there. The elementary inequality $(s+t)^2\le2(s^2+t^2)$, which follows from $(s-t)^2\ge0$, and integration give $\left\|v_0+\sum_kv_k\right\|_A^2 \le2\left(\|v_0\|_A^2+\sum_k\|v_k\|_A^2\right).$ Hence $C_1\le2$. [given, algebra]

3.1 Apply [F1] to the exact Schwarz data [F2] with $C_0\le2$ and $C_1\le2$ to obtain $\kappa_A(BA)\le4$. This finite one-dimensional split has a global coarse space; higher-dimensional overlap estimates are handled separately on the A page. [F1, F2, step 2.2, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

Let $N=2M$ with $M\ge2$ on the uniform fine P1 Dirichlet mesh of $(0,1)$.
Take the coarse P1 space on the even nodes and one local space
$\operatorname{span}\{\phi_{2k-1}\}$ for each odd node. The exact two-level
additive Schwarz operator has $C_0\le2$, $C_1\le2$, and hence
$\kappa_A(BA)\le4$, independently of $M$.

1.2 On each fine interval, at most one odd nodal hat has nonzero derivative. Thus only the coarse derivative and at most one local derivative can be nonzero there. The elementary inequality $(s+t)^2\le2(s^2+t^2)$, which follows from $(s-t)^2\ge0$, and integration give $\left\|v_0+\sum_kv_k\right\|_A^2 \le2\left(\|v_0\|_A^2+\sum_k\|v_k\|_A^2\right).$ Hence $C_1\le2$. [given, algebra]

2.2 Since $\eta_k=(a_k-b_k)/2$ and $(a_k-b_k)^2\le2(a_k^2+b_k^2)$, the local energy is $\|u_k\|_A^2=2\eta_k^2/h\le(a_k^2+b_k^2)/h$. Summing gives $\sum_k\|u_k\|_A^2\le\|u\|_A^2$. The decomposition in step 1.1 therefore has total energy at most $2\|u\|_A^2$, so $C_0\le2$. [step 1.1, algebra]

## Example

Take two adjacent unit-square subdomains, each split by the diagonal from its southwest to its northeast corner into two affine triangles, and put coefficient $\rho=1$. Before outer Dirichlet values are imposed, each local floating stiffness matrix in the cyclic vertex order $(a,b,c,d)$ is

$$K_i=\tfrac12\begin{pmatrix}2&-1&0&-1\\-1&2&-1&0\\0&-1&2&-1\\-1&0&-1&2\end{pmatrix}.$$

The two interface endpoints are primal corners. Impose homogeneous Dirichlet data on the full top exterior side of the two-square domain, a nonempty segment that is a union of mesh sides. The local constant modes are thereby anchored, and the shared primal corners enforce their common interface values; after exact interior elimination, the assembled Schur solve is the original finite-element problem.

2.1 The displayed matrix has zero row sums, and its quadratic form is $\tfrac12[(u_a-u_b)^2+(u_b-u_c)^2+(u_c-u_d)^2+(u_d-u_a)^2]$. It is therefore nonnegative with kernel exactly the constant vector, agreeing with [F2]. [given, step 1.1, F2, algebra]

3.1 The imposed zero values on each subdomain's top exterior side fix its local constant mode; equality at the shared primal endpoints also enforces interface continuity. Thus [F3] gives an invertible partially assembled solve. Theorem [F4] then identifies the condensed interface solution and harmonic reconstruction with the original global finite-element solution. [given, F3, F4, step 2.1] ∎

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. For positive-area convex polygons $P,Q\subset\mathbb R^2$ with rational vertices, [[alg-certified-convex-polygon-overlap]] terminates and returns exactly $P\cap Q$ as a cyclic list of rational vertices, with its exact Lebesgue area. Empty intersections and intersections consisting only of a point or segment return area zero. The result can be used as the exact weight $|P\cap Q|$ in [[def-intersection-volume-conservative-remapping]].

1.1 Clearing one common positive denominator from the three rational points in an orientation test multiplies the determinant by a positive square, so its sign is unchanged and all scaled coordinates are integers. Therefore [F2] returns the exact side classification, including boundary zero, for every clipping pass. [F1, F2, given, algebra]

2.1 The algorithm's finite certificate accepts only a simple counterclockwise cycle whose vertices lie in the closed left half-plane of every directed edge, with any collinear consecutive triple ordered monotonically. Each edge is therefore a supporting boundary segment of the convex hull of the listed vertices; the simple closed cycle with positive area traverses that hull boundary once, so the certified input is the stated convex polygon. Now fix one directed edge of $Q$ and write $s(X)$ for its signed edge determinant. If $s(S),s(E)\ge0$, the whole segment remains and the traversal appends $E$. If $s(S)\ge0>s(E)$, it appends the crossing point; if $s(S)<0\le s(E)$, it appends the crossing point and $E$; and if both signs are negative, it appends nothing. In either crossing case, $s(S)-s(E)$ has the strict sign of the crossing and is nonzero, and $t=s(S)/(s(S)-s(E))$ lies in $[0,1]$. If an endpoint lies on the clipping line, the formula gives that endpoint exactly. Thus each pass returns the cyclic boundary of the preceding convex intersection with this closed half-plane, preserving isolated boundary vertices and degenerate point or segment outputs. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

## Statement

Let $Q=(0,1)^d$, $0<\lambda\le a\le\Lambda$ be scalar and periodic, and let $f\in L^2(Q)$. For each $\epsilon>0$, let $u_\epsilon\in H^1_0(Q)$ solve the oscillatory weak equation with coefficient $a(x/\epsilon)$, and suppose $u_0\in C^2(\overline Q)\cap H^1_0(Q)$ solves the homogenized equation with the same datum $f$. For $0<\epsilon\le1/4$ choose a Lipschitz cutoff $\eta_\epsilon$ equal to zero where $\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial Q)\le\epsilon$, equal to one where that distance is at least $2\epsilon$, and with $|\nabla\eta_\epsilon|\le C_d/\epsilon$. Define
$$w_\epsilon(x)=u_0(x)+\epsilon\eta_\epsilon(x)\sum_{j=1}^d\chi_j(x/\epsilon)\partial_ju_0(x).$$
Then $w_\epsilon\in H^1_0(Q)$ and, for a constant independent of $\epsilon$,
$$\|\nabla(u_\epsilon-w_\epsilon)\|_{L^2(Q)}+\|u_\epsilon-u_0\|_{L^2(Q)}\le C\sqrt\epsilon.$$
The constant may depend on $d,\lambda,\Lambda$, the fixed corrector and flux-potential $H^1(Y)$ norms, $\|u_0\|_{C^2(\overline Q)}$, and the cutoff profile. No rate is asserted without this regularity and periodicity.

1.1 Let $	heta(s)=0$ for $s\le1$, $	heta(s)=1$ for $s\ge2$, and linear on $[1,2]$, and set $\eta_\epsilon(x)=	heta(\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial Q)/\epsilon)$. Distance to a closed set is $1$-Lipschitz, so this cutoff has the required gradient bound. Set $U_\epsilon=u_0+\epsilon\sum_j\chi_j(x/\epsilon)g_j(x)$ with $g_j=\partial_ju_0$. For each corrector, its defining smooth periodic approximants converge in $H^1$ on any bounded union of period cells, since that union meets only finitely many cells. Applying the affine pullback rule [F8] with $y=x/\epsilon$ shows $\chi_j(x/\epsilon)\in H^1(Q)$ with weak gradient $\epsilon^{-1}
abla_y\chi_j(x/\epsilon)$. Multiplication by $g_j\in C^1(\overline Q)$ preserves $H^1$: apply the classical product rule to the smooth periodic approximants and pass in $H^1$, using the boundedness of $g_j$ and $
abla g_j$. The cutoff correction in $w_\epsilon$ vanishes in a neighborhood of $\partial Q$, while $u_0\in H^1_0(Q)$; hence $w_\epsilon\in H^1_0(Q)$. Existence and uniqueness of $u_\epsilon$ follow from [F7]. Differentiating the uncut expression by the weak chain and product rules gives $a(x/\epsilon)
abla U_\epsilon=A^*
abla u_0+\sum_jq^j(x/\epsilon)g_j+\epsilon a(x/\epsilon)\sum_j\chi_j(x/\epsilon)
abla g_j.$ Subtract the homogenized weak equation for $u_0$. [F7, F1, F2, F3, F4, F8, A1, algebra]

abla_y\chi_j(x/\epsilon)$. Multiplication by $g_j\in C^1(\overline Q)$ preserves $H^1$: apply the classical product rule to the smooth periodic approximants and pass in $H^1$, using the boundedness of $g_j$ and $
abla g_j$. The cutoff correction in $w_\epsilon$ vanishes in a neighborhood of $\partial Q$, while $u_0\in H^1_0(Q)$; hence $w_\epsilon\in H^1_0(Q)$. 2.2 Let $S_{2\epsilon}=\{x\in Q:\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial Q)<2\epsilon\}$. abla(w_\epsilon-U_\epsilon)\|_2\le C\sqrt\epsilon$: the three product-rule terms are bounded respectively by $C\|
abla\chi_j(\cdot/\epsilon)\|_{L^2(S)}$, $C\epsilon\|\chi_j(\cdot/\epsilon)\|_{L^2(S)}$, and $C\epsilon\|
abla\eta_\epsilon\|_\infty\|\chi_j(\cdot/\epsilon)\|_{L^2(S)}$. [F2, step 1.1, algebra]

## Statement

On the Delaunay triangle with vertices $(0,0),(2,0),(0,2)$ and vertex data $0,2,2$, the query $(1/2,1/2)$ has barycentric weights $1/2,1/4,1/4$ and affine interpolated value $1$.

1.1 Let $\lambda_0,\lambda_1,\lambda_2$ correspond to $(0,0),(2,0),(0,2)$. The coordinate equations give $2\lambda_1=1/2$ and $2\lambda_2=1/2$, hence $\lambda_1=\lambda_2=1/4$; their sum constraint gives $\lambda_0=1/2$. All three are nonnegative, so the query lies in the triangle by [F3]. [given, F1, F3, algebra]

## Statement

For BDDC and FETI-DP built from the same positive definite partially assembled Schur operator, primal constraints, and scaled averaging, all eigenvalues of the two preconditioned operators other than $1$ agree with multiplicity. With the multiplier space fixed as $\Lambda=\operatorname{range}B$, neither operator has a zero eigenvalue; retaining all redundant row coordinates instead would add only multiplier null modes that are removed by this convention. The multiplicity of $1$ is not asserted to agree.

2.1 Apply [F3] to conclude equal eigenvalues and multiplicities for every eigenvalue other than $1$. The identities $E_0R=I$ and $BB_D^T=I$ make $R$ and $B_D^T$ injective and $E_0$ and $B$ surjective onto their ranges; since $\widetilde S$ is positive definite, the four Gram operators in the two products are positive definite on their respective spaces. Thus both preconditioned products have positive eigenvalues. Taking $\Lambda=\operatorname{range}B$ removes redundant multiplier null modes. No step determines the multiplicity of eigenvalue $1$. [given, F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Let $n\ge1$, $0\le d<n$, and $x_0<\cdots<x_n$ be real nodes in
$[a,b]=[x_0,x_n]$. Put
$h=\max_{0\le j<n}(x_{j+1}-x_j)$, $m=n-d$, and
$\epsilon=1$ if $m$ is even and $\epsilon=0$ if $m$ is odd. Let
$f\in C^{d+1}([a,b])$, set $g=f^{(d+1)}$, and suppose $g$ has finite total
variation $V=\operatorname{Var}_{[a,b]}(g)$ as defined in
[[def-bounded-variation-and-total-variation]]. For a continuous $q$ on
$[a,b]$, write $\|q\|_\infty=\sup_{x\in[a,b]}|q(x)|$. If $d\ge1$, then
$$\|f-r_d\|_\infty \le \frac{h^{d+1}}{d+1}\bigl(V+\epsilon\|g\|_\infty\bigr),$$
If $d=0$, let $\beta$ be the local mesh ratio in
[[def-floater-hormann-local-mesh-ratio]]. Then
$$\|f-r_0\|_\infty\le h(1+\beta)\bigl(V+\epsilon\|f'\|_\infty\bigr).$$
No mesh-ratio restriction is needed when $d\ge1$. For $d=0$, a fixed global
mesh-ratio bound $\rho=h/h_{\min}$ implies $\beta\le\rho$ by
[[lem-floater-hormann-local-mesh-ratio-bounded-by-global]].

1.1 By [F9], $d+1\in\mathbb N$. Fix $x$ in an open node gap. By [F7], the derivatives in [F1] exist and are continuous. By [F1], $f(x)-r_d(x)=N(x)/D(x)$ with $N(x)=\sum_{i=0}^{m}(-1)^iG_i$. [F10] makes the derivative sup norm in the statement finite. Pair successive terms as $(G_0-G_1)+(G_2-G_3)+\cdots$. The sum of the absolute values of these pair differences is bounded by the full adjacent-increment sum in [F2], hence by $V/(d+1)!$. If $m$ is even there is one unpaired term $G_m$; otherwise there is none. [given, F1, F2, F9, F10, algebra]

4.1 At every node the error is zero by [F5]. Since $r_d$ has no real poles, $f-r_d$ is continuous on the compact interval and has a finite supremum by [F10]. The estimates on the open gaps therefore imply the stated supremum bounds. If $f\in C^{d+2}$, then for any partition [F8] gives $|g(t_{i+1})-g(t_i)|\le\|f^{(d+2)}\|_\infty(t_{i+1}-t_i)$; summing and taking the supremum yields $V\le(b-a)\|f^{(d+2)}\|_\infty$. [given, F5, F6, F7, F8, F10, step 3.1, step 3.2, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Let $\Pi_h:H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^d)\to V_h$ be the MINI Fortin map constructed in [[thm-na-mini-element-fortin-stability]]. On every shape-regular matching mesh, there is a constant $C$ independent of $h$ such that
$$\|v-\Pi_hv\|_{L^2(D)}\le Ch\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(D)}\qquad(v\in H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^d)).$$
For every fixed $v\in H^1_0(D)^d$, $\Pi_hv\to v$ in $H^1_0$ as $h\to0$. If $v\in V_\sigma$, exact Fortin preservation also gives $\Pi_hv\in Z_h$.

1.3 Let $v\in C_c^\infty(D)^d$ and extend it by zero to $\mathbb R^d$. On each cell $K$, choose a vertex $x_K$ and let $p_K$ be the affine Taylor polynomial of $v$ there. Every selected facet used in $I_h$ for a vertex of $K$ lies within $Ch_K$ of $x_K$ by the patch geometry in the face-average interpolation supplier. Apply [F6] on the convex open set $\mathbb R^d$; the pointwise Taylor error on those facets is at most $Ch_K^2\|D^2v\|_\infty$. The scaled dual moments in [F5] then bound the coefficients of $I_h(v-p_K)$ on $K$ by the same amount. ## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be bounded, connected and polyhedral, $d=2$ or $3$. Let $\mathcal T_j$ be matching shape-regular meshes with $h_j\to0$, let $Z_j$ be the weak MINI divergence kernels, and let $0=t_0^j<\cdots<t_{N_j}^j=T$ have maximum step tending to zero. Suppose $U_j^n\in Z_j$, their piecewise-constant reconstructions $\overline U_j$ satisfy
$$\sup_j\left(\max_n\|U_j^n\|_{L^2}+\|\overline U_j\|_{L^2(0,T;H^1_0)}\right)<\infty,$$
and the following coefficient condition holds: for every finite $L^2$-orthonormal family $e_1,\ldots,e_m\in V_\sigma$, the $E$-valued piecewise-constant functions
$$Y_j(t)=\sum_{i=1}^m(U_j^n,\Pi_je_i)_{L^2}e_i\quad(t\in(t_{n-1}^j,t_n^j])$$
have uniformly bounded $L^2(0,T;E)$ norms and their backward difference quotients are bounded in $L^{4/3}(0,T;E)$; here $\Pi_j$ is the MINI Fortin map and $E=\operatorname{span}\{e_i\}$. Then $(\overline U_j)$ is relatively compact in $L^2(0,T;L^2(D)^d)$.

3.1 Let $P_E$ be the $L^2$-orthogonal projection. On times when $\|\overline U_j(t)\|_V\le R$, step 2.1 gives $\|\overline U_j-P_E\overline U_j\|_2\le\epsilon$. The measure of the remaining times is at most $R^{-2}\|\overline U_j\|_{L^2V}^2$, and there $\|\overline U_j-P_E\overline U_j\|_2\le2\sup_{j,n}\|U_j^n\|_2$. First choose $R$ large, then $\epsilon$ small; this makes the $L^2(0,T;L^2)$ projection remainder uniformly small for sufficiently large $j$. [given, step 2.1, algebra]
